```{r}
#| include: false
root <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("renv.lock"))
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root)
for (f in setdiff(list.files(file.path(root, "R"), pattern = "[.]R$"), "_dependencies.R")) source(file.path(root, "R", f))
d <- targets::tar_read(e2_report_data, store = file.path(root, "_targets"))
s <- d$summary
names_of <- c(FULL = "Full data (reference)", MMRM = "MMRM, all observed", MI_J2R = "MI, jump to reference (A1)", MI_MAR = "MI, missing at random (S1)")
s$analysis_label <- names_of[s$analysis]
s$mechanism <- factor(s$mechanism, levels = unique(d$cells$mechanism))
f2 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3)
f1 <- function(x) formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = 1)
```

::: {.callout-note}
**Simulated data · fictional compound.** FJF-2026 does not exist. The trials of this study are generated by code from the **planning values** of the design assumptions with public seeds. The sealed truth and the simulator are not used (ADR 0018). The plan, `docs/sap/e2-simulation-plan.yml` (ADR 0036), was committed before any result was computed.
:::

# Question and design

The primary analysis of FJF-2026-301 imputes the values of patients who leave the study by jump to reference; the supplementary analysis is a mixed model for repeated measures under missing at random. How do they, and imputation under missing at random, behave when who leaves depends on the outcome?

- **Target:** the treatment-policy difference between FJF-2026 20 mg and placebo in the change of HbA1c at week 26, in the full data. Its value, from a trial of `r d$plan$truth$per_arm` patients per arm of the same generator, is **`r f2(d$truth$value)`** (Monte Carlo error `r f2(d$truth$se)`). Negative means a larger reduction on FJF-2026.
- **Trials:** 150 patients per arm, `r d$plan$trials_per_cell` per cell, `r d$plan$imputations` imputations, one public seed per trial.
- **Cells:** `r length(unique(s$cell))`, every mechanism at a dropout rate of 6% (the planning value) and of 15% (a stress value outside the truth range of the assumption).
- **Mechanisms:** `r paste(vapply(d$plan$dropout$mechanisms, function(m) paste0(m$id, " (", m$note, ")"), ""), collapse = "; ")`.
- **Reference:** the "Full data" row is the estimate had nothing been missing. It has no bias by construction; its bias and its Monte Carlo error show how much of any other bias is noise.

# Results

The Monte Carlo error of a bias is `empirical sd / sqrt(trials)`, about `r f2(median(s$bias_mcse))`: a bias smaller than twice that cannot be told from zero.

```{r}
#| results: asis
tab <- s[, c("mechanism", "rate", "analysis_label", "bias", "bias_mcse", "empirical_sd", "mean_se", "coverage", "power", "failed")]
tab$rate <- paste0(100 * tab$rate, "%")
tab$bias <- f2(tab$bias)
tab$bias_mcse <- f2(tab$bias_mcse)
tab$empirical_sd <- f2(tab$empirical_sd)
tab$mean_se <- f2(tab$mean_se)
tab$coverage <- f1(tab$coverage)
tab$power <- f1(tab$power)
names(tab) <- c("Mechanism", "Dropout", "Analysis", "Bias", "MC error", "Empirical SD", "Mean model SE", "Coverage (%)", "Power (%)", "Failed")
print(knitr::kable(tab, align = "llrrrrrrrr", row.names = FALSE))
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 9
library(ggplot2)
shown <- s[s$analysis != "FULL", ]
shown$cell_label <- paste0(shown$mechanism, ", ", 100 * shown$rate, "%")
ggplot(shown, aes(bias, cell_label, colour = analysis_label)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = bias - 2 * bias_mcse, xmax = bias + 2 * bias_mcse), position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  labs(x = "Bias against the treatment-policy target (HbA1c points; +/- 2 Monte Carlo errors)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Expectations of the plan, checked

The plan stated three expectations before the results. "Nearly unbiased" is made precise here as an absolute bias below 0.05 HbA1c points, and "overstates the benefit" as a bias below -0.05. Both thresholds are written in this report's code, not tuned to the results.

```{r}
#| results: asis
near <- function(x) abs(x) < 0.05
get <- function(mech, rate, an) s[s$mechanism == mech & s$rate == rate & s$analysis == an, ]
rows <- list()
add <- function(text, ok) rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <<- data.frame(Expectation = text, Result = ifelse(ok, "Met", "Not met"))
low <- d$plan$dropout$rates[[1]]$rate
high <- d$plan$dropout$rates[[2]]$rate
for (m in c("MCAR", "MAR")) for (an in c("MMRM", "MI_MAR")) {
  add(sprintf("%s, 6%% and 15%%: %s nearly unbiased", m, names_of[[an]]), near(get(m, low, an)$bias) && near(get(m, high, an)$bias))
}
for (m in c("MNAR_MOD", "MNAR_STR")) for (an in c("MMRM", "MI_MAR")) {
  add(sprintf("%s at 15%%: %s overstates the benefit", m, names_of[[an]]), get(m, high, an)$bias < -0.05)
}
add("MNAR_ACT at 15%: jump to reference is less optimistic than the MAR analyses",
    get("MNAR_ACT", high, "MI_J2R")$bias > max(get("MNAR_ACT", high, "MMRM")$bias, get("MNAR_ACT", high, "MI_MAR")$bias))
print(knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, rows), row.names = FALSE))
```

# What the results say

```{r}
#| results: asis
j <- s[s$analysis == "MI_J2R", ]
m <- s[s$analysis == "MMRM", ]
cat(sprintf(
  "- **Jump to reference** has a bias between %s and %s across the cells; it is above the target (less benefit) in %d of %d cells. It assumes the effect is lost on leaving, which the target (treatment policy with the generator's fading effect) only partly does.\n",
  f2(min(j$bias)), f2(max(j$bias)), sum(j$bias > 0), nrow(j)))
cat(sprintf(
  "- **MMRM on all observed values** has a bias between %s and %s; the largest is at %s, %s%%.\n",
  f2(min(m$bias)), f2(max(m$bias)), m$mechanism[which.max(abs(m$bias))], 100 * m$rate[which.max(abs(m$bias))]))
cov <- s[s$analysis != "FULL", ]
cat(sprintf(
  "- **Coverage** of the 95%% intervals runs from %s%% to %s%% (Monte Carlo error about %s points); the lowest is %s, %s%%, for %s.\n",
  f1(min(cov$coverage)), f1(max(cov$coverage)), f1(median(cov$coverage_mcse)),
  cov$mechanism[which.min(cov$coverage)], 100 * cov$rate[which.min(cov$coverage)], names_of[[cov$analysis[which.min(cov$coverage)]]]))
cat(sprintf("- **Failures:** %d analyses did not converge or failed in %d trials.\n", sum(s$failed), sum(s$trials)))
```

# Reading of the results

```{r}
#| results: asis
act <- s[s$mechanism == "MNAR_ACT" & s$rate == high & s$analysis %in% c("MMRM", "MI_MAR", "MI_J2R"), ]
both <- s[s$mechanism %in% c("MNAR_MOD", "MNAR_STR") & s$analysis %in% c("MMRM", "MI_MAR"), ]
cat(sprintf(
  "- **The expectation about MNAR dropout in both arms was not met.** When the dependence on the unobserved change is the same in both arms, the two missing-at-random analyses have a bias between %s and %s, which is at most %s Monte Carlo errors. Patients with a worse change leave in both arms, the selection shifts both arm means in the same direction, and most of it cancels in the difference between arms.\n",
  f2(min(both$bias)), f2(max(both$bias)), formatC(max(abs(both$bias) / both$bias_mcse), format = "f", digits = 1)))
cat(sprintf(
  "- **MNAR in the active arm only is where the missing-at-random analyses fail.** At %s%% they overstate the benefit by %s (MMRM) and %s (imputation under missing at random), and their coverage falls to %s%% and %s%%. Jump to reference has a bias of %s there.\n",
  100 * high, f2(-act$bias[act$analysis == "MMRM"]), f2(-act$bias[act$analysis == "MI_MAR"]),
  f1(act$coverage[act$analysis == "MMRM"]), f1(act$coverage[act$analysis == "MI_MAR"]), f2(act$bias[act$analysis == "MI_J2R"])))
cat(sprintf(
  "- **Jump to reference trades bias for safety.** Under MCAR and MAR it is biased towards less benefit, by %s at 6%% and %s at 15%% dropout, because it assumes the effect is lost on leaving; its power falls from %s%% to %s%% (MCAR). In exchange it is the one analysis that does not overstate the benefit when dropout depends on the outcome in the active arm only.\n",
  f2(j$bias[j$mechanism == "MCAR" & j$rate == low]), f2(j$bias[j$mechanism == "MCAR" & j$rate == high]),
  f1(j$power[j$mechanism == "MCAR" & j$rate == low]), f1(j$power[j$mechanism == "MCAR" & j$rate == high])))
```

- **The reference row carries the error of the target.** The full-data estimate has a bias of about its own Monte Carlo error plus that of the target (`r f2(d$truth$se)`), so biases smaller than about 0.02 are noise.

# Limits

- The conclusions hold for this generator. Its mechanisms are chosen to be understood, not to resemble a real trial, and the outcome-dependent mechanism is a logistic one.
- The target is the treatment-policy value of this generator, in which the effect fades after discontinuation over 12 weeks. A different assumption about what happens after leaving would change what jump to reference should be compared with.
- The imputation seeds and trial seeds are public and fixed; a different seed changes every figure by about its Monte Carlo error.
- Both programs and the plan have the same author.
